parsed.why: Comprehensive statutory trans protections, self-ID recognition accepted, hate-crime coverage, high freedom index, tolerant society; the one trans killing was prosecuted. Enforcement uneven and no non-binary marker, but no universal visitor-facing restriction is documented.

No recognition machinery, employment-only protection, vague morality provisions usable against public conduct, pervasive documented social and religious intolerance, LGBT organisations barred. No documented trans-specific violence, but thin data plus no recourse warrants cautious high-risk extrapolation.

2026 recognition narrowing plus real document friction: airport stop despite ID, demanded passport medical exam, railway police gender checks and custody mistreatment. Offset by constitutional equality, high-court relief and police abuse assessed as non-systemic; uneven subnational protections.

No criminalisation and national gender-identity discrimination and hate-speech laws, with police protecting the capital's Pride. Against that: documented hate-speech surge, physical attacks on a gender-nonconforming person, uneven penalty enhancements, constitutionally entrenched social hostility.

2024 package bans gender-marker change, transition care, Pride and rainbow displays; a trans woman was murdered days after passage; police have arrested Pride victims, declared events impossible, and hate-crime law is documented as unenforced.
